thread.title: Market Snapshot: Stocks trade lower after Trump says ‘highly unlikely’ he would hold off on raising China tariffs

author: Stocks News Feed
title: Market Snapshot: Stocks trade lower after Trump says ‘highly unlikely’ he would hold off on raising China tariffs
text:
Stocks fell Tuesday, after remarks from President Donald Trump stoked fresh anxieties about the prospects of a near-term resolution of trade tensions between the U.S. and China.
How are benchmarks performing? The Dow Jones Industrial Average
 YMZ8, +0.01%
 was down 145 points, or 0.6%, at 24,496. The S&P 500 index
 SPX, +0.02%
 fell 8.16 points, or 0.3%, to 2,662, while the Nasdaq Composite Index
 COMP, +0.17%
 was off 22.6 points at 7,060, a decline of 0.3%.
On Monday, the Dow climbed 354.29 points, or 1.5%, to 24,640.24, while the S&P 500 rose 40.89 points, or 1.6%, to 2,673.45. The Nasdaq Composite Index rallied 142.87 points, or 2.1%, to 7,081.85.
What’s driving the market? Trump told The Wall Street Journal, in an interview published late Monday, that it is “highly unlikely” that he would accept Beijing’s request to hold off on increasing tariff rates on Chinese goods from the beginning of January 2019, raising some doubts about prospects for a detente between the world’s two largest economic superpowers when Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping meet on Friday in Buenos Aires. The pair are set to discuss trade on the sidelines of a meeting of the Group of 20 nations.
Trump said that if talks with his Chinese counterpart don’t go well that he could put tariffs on the rest of Chinese imports that are currently not subject to duties. “If we don’t make a deal, then I’m going to put the $267 billion additional on” at a tariff rate of either 10% or 25%, he told WSJ.
Animosities over trade between the U.S. and China have been among the central concerns for investors recently because an intensification of hostilities could precipitate a slowdown in China and the rest of the world.
Investors are also digesting comments from Federal Reserve No. 2 Richard Clarida, who continued to present a relatively dovish stance in a Monday morning speech to a conference sponsored by The Clearing House in New York, ahead of a Fed policy meeting later this month, when the central bank is widely expected to raise interest rates.
Market participants, however, are eager for more clarity as to the Fed’s plan for interest rate increases in 2019, and on this point, Clarida said incoming data “supports the case for gradual policy normalization” next year, while emphasizing that the federal-funds rate much closer to the “neutral level,” at which the Fed will stop raising rates, than it was when it began hiking in 2015. “How close is a matter of judgment, and there is a range of views on the FOMC,” he said.

Which stocks are in focus? Apple Inc . shares
 AAPL, -0.38%
 were in focus after Trump said during The Wall Street Journal interview t hat tariffs could also be placed on iPhones and laptop computers imported from China if the U.S. decides to put tariffs on additional goods. Shares of Apple were down 0.9% Tuesday morning.
Chip makers are also facing selling pressure Tuesday, as new or magnified tariffs are expected to hurt sales and raise input costs. Shares of Nvidia Corp .
 NVDA, +0.30%
 are down 0.9% while shares of Analog Devices, Inc .
 ADI, -0.22%
 have fallen 1.3%.
Microsoft Corp .
 MSFT, +0.40%
 shares are in focus as the software giant guns for the chance to claim the title of the world’s largest company. The software-and-services firm closed Monday with a market capitalization just $11 billion, or 1.3%, shy of Apple’s, currently the world’s largest firm by market value. Microsoft shares were down 0.3%.
United Technologies Corp .
 UTX, -5.77%
 on Monday announced that it planned on breaking its company in to three parts. Shares were down 6%.
Shares of General Motors Co .
 GM, -0.58%
 were on the decline, a day after it closed at a three-month high following the announcement of cost-cutting measures that included layoffs and plant closures. Trump on Monday ripped GM’s plans , telling the Journal he told Barra she should stop making cars in China and replace lost production in Ohio. GM’s stock was down 1.3% early Tuesday.
Tiffany & Co .
 TIF, +0.07%
 stock was down 2%, ahead of the jewelry merchant’s third-quarter earnings report to be released before the market open Wednesday. The stock has been under pressure in recent weeks as a supply glut for low-end diamonds has forced prices to fall.
Shares of Bristol-Myers Squibb Co .
 BMY, -3.80%
 declined 4.8%, after the company reported the failure of a study of a prospective skin-cancer drug Monday evening.
What are strategists saying? “Psychology is the main force driving markets lower,” Matt Lloyd, chief investment strategist at Advisors Asset Management, told MarketWatch. “We’re a bunch of long-tailed cats in a room full of rocking chairs” waiting for the worst to happen, he said.
While an escalating trade war could hurt some corporate profits, Lloyd said, other factors, like low unemployment, rising wages, and a resilient global economy — as evidenced by 80% of purchasing manager surveys around the world indicating improving economic conditions — should overwhelm trade headwinds, Lloyd argued.
“As for Apple, and the impact from possible tariffs…any negative effects are likely to be overstated given that the firm was able to absorb the impact of lifting the ceiling price on its most expensive iPhone model by much more than that with its recent upgrades,” wrote Michael Hewson, chief market strategist at CMC Markets UK, in a note.
What data and other Fed speakers are ahead? Home prices across the country are rising at the slowest pace in nearly two years , according to the S&P/Case-Chiller 20-city Index, released Wednesday morning.
Meanwhile, Atlanta Federal Reserve Bank President Raphael Bostic, Kansas Federal Reserve Bank President Esther George and Chicago Federal Reserve Bank President Charles Evans will participate in a panel discussion and Q&A at 2:30 p.m. at the Clearing House Conference in New York.
How are other markets trading? Asian markets started strong Tuesday , but cooled on fears over rising U.S.-China trade tensions. Japan’s Nikkei
 NIK, +0.64%
 rose 0.6%, but Hong Kong‘s Hang Seng Index
 HSI, -0.17%
 finished down 0.2%, while China’s Shanghai Composite Index
 SHCOMP, -0.04%
 also made an about face to end the day slightly lower.
European markets declined Tuesday , with the Stoxx Europe 600
 SXXP, -0.21%
 falling 0.6%, while Germany’s DAX
 DAX, +0.00%
 and France’s CAC 40
 PX1, -0.14%
 are also edging lower. The FTSE 100
 UKX, -0.20%
 was down 0.6%.
Crude oil
 CLF9, +0.56%
 is up 0.4% Tuesday , one day after it notched its best single-day rise in 8 weeks . Gold
 GCZ8, -0.75%
 was on track for a third straight losing session , while the U.S. dollar
 DXY, +0.35%
 saw a modest rise .
